reply.thought: The handoff says Alpha's refunds are complete and the applied list matches the requested list. I should verify against the shared ledger before paying anyone, starting with list_refunds.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's applied list and the signed batch request exactly. Before paying, I'll check the orders so I know which customers are owed what and can confirm the refunds reference real orders.

The ledger refunds match Alpha's applied list and the signed batch request, and each refund references a real order and is less than that order's amount. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 54385 matches my check: orders 200 and 203 total 73072, less the 18687 refund on order 203. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 29147 matches my check: orders 201 and 204 total 44020, less refunds of 3873 and 11000. Cobalt is the last customer with orders, so I'll get its net balance.

All three net balances match my independent check against the orders and refunds, and the ledger refunds match Alpha's applied list and signed request. No problem found, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme's 54385.
Acme's payout of 54385 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 29147 matches my independent check, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 29147 was recorded. Cobalt's net balance of 33079 matches my check: orders 202 and 205 total 33079, with no refunds against them. Recording the last payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches my independent check against the orders and refunds. The task is complete.
